objective: Consolidate standalone todo functionality and workflow-backed work projection into the pi-swe extension so one reliable todo surface operates standalone or delegates active workflow mutations to SweService without duplicate task authority.

in: Move the existing branch-backed todo core and public todo surface under pi-swe
Introduce a provider-neutral todo view/backend contract
Add a workflow-backed provider that projects workflow.json and routes legal mutations through SweService
Replace duplicate todo/SWE docket and modal implementations with one capability-driven UI
Make pi-swe the sole registration point for both swe and todo commands/tools
Remove obsolete optional lifecycle bridging and independent pi-todo extension discovery
Preserve existing branch todo entries and public todo behavior in standalone mode
Update tests, documentation, anatomy, catalog, and inventory
out: Changing workflow.json schema version or weakening its validation and evidence gates
Copying workflow work into standalone todo session state
Allowing todo finish to bypass implemented, verification, review, or completion gates
Committing or pushing changes without separate authorization

constraints: workflow.json remains the sole planning authority whenever a focused active initiative owns the todo surface
Standalone branch entries remain the sole authority outside active workflow mode
Backend selection must be deterministic and reread current workflow authority before mutation
Existing todo session entries must remain readable without migration
Unsupported workflow structural mutations must fail with guidance to use intentional swe revision
Exactly one todo command and tool may be registered

acceptanceCriteria.text: Loading pi-swe alone exposes the existing standalone todo command, structured tool, persistence behavior, and modal functionality without requiring pi-todo.
A focused active initiative is rendered directly from workflow.json through the todo surface, and legal lifecycle actions mutate only through SweService.
Standalone and workflow state are never synchronized or duplicated, and deterministic switching preserves inactive standalone state.
One shared capability-driven docket and modal represent standalone and workflow states including hierarchy, readiness, phases, and distinct implemented versus complete states.
The independent pi-todo registration and optional lifecycle bridge are removed without duplicate registrations or regressions in supported command and tool behavior.
Typecheck, todo tests, SWE tests, full tests, repository checks, and release verification pass with current evidence.

assessment.reason: This consolidation changes extension discovery, state authority selection, persistence compatibility, lifecycle routing, public tool behavior, and two interactive UI implementations.
unknowns: Whether all existing todo public result shapes can remain byte-compatible while exposing workflow-specific statuses
Which paused and draft workflow states should be visible versus actionable through todo
Whether lifecycle coordination has consumers outside pi-swe and pi-todo

practices.reason: Existing standalone todo branch persistence and public behavior must survive relocation unchanged.
Workflow projection must avoid a second ledger and preserve SweService mutation and evidence boundaries.
The duplicate modals and dockets should converge behind a provider-neutral view without losing domain distinctions.
Single registration, metadata consistency, compatibility, and removal of the old extension require repository-wide checks.
Completion requires current machine evidence across focused and repository-wide verification surfaces.

obligations.text: Characterize existing branch entry hydration, standalone mutations, public outputs, and ownership behavior before relocating implementation.
Relocate standalone todo code under pi-swe while preserving event formats and supported command/tool semantics.
Verify active workflow projection reads workflow.json and routes start and finish-as-implemented through SweService without standalone writes.
Verify one shared modal and renderer cover standalone and workflow hierarchy, capabilities, readiness, and statuses.
Verify pi-swe registers todo exactly once and obsolete extension bridging and discovery are removed with regenerated metadata.
Run typecheck, focused suites, full tests, checks, and release verification against the final bounded source set.

decisions.text: Todo is a capability owned and registered by pi-swe rather than a peer extension.
decisions.basis: This removes optional extension ordering and duplicated interactive surfaces while preserving standalone functionality.

decisions.text: Workflow mode projects current workflow authority and never mirrors work into branch todo entries.
decisions.basis: workflow.json must remain the only workflow task ledger.

decisions.text: Todo finish maps to implemented in workflow mode, never complete.
decisions.basis: SWE completion remains verification, review, and evidence gated.

decisions.text: Workflow structural actions unsupported by an exact legal service operation remain disabled and direct users to swe revise.
decisions.basis: Generic todo CRUD must not bypass intentional revision rationale or compare-and-swap integrity.

risks.text: Moving the standalone core could make historic branch todo entries unreadable.
risks.mitigation: Preserve entry discriminants and payloads and add fixture-based compatibility tests before relocation.

risks.text: A cached backend could mutate stale or incorrect authority after initiative transitions.
risks.mitigation: Resolve backend and reread workflow status for each operation and modal opening.

risks.text: A generic status model could erase the difference between implemented and complete.
risks.mitigation: Carry provider-specific raw status and capability metadata through the view model.

risks.text: Both old and new extension entrypoints could register duplicate todo commands or tools.
risks.mitigation: Add registration-count tests and remove independent discovery atomically.

risks.text: Broad UI refactoring could regress terminal keyboard, scrolling, and rendering behavior.
risks.mitigation: Retain existing characterization tests and add provider-specific shared UI coverage.
